title: Why this sphere exists
summary: ooRexx is a niche language relative to what most LLMs were trained on. Its specific traps do not look like traps -- they compile cleanly, run without a crash, and produce a plausible-but-wrong result or a confusing crash several layers away from the actual mistake. This sphere is deliberately narrow: every rule and article in it is grounded in a real incident from this project's own development, not a general survey of the language.
invariants: Nothing in this sphere is included on the strength of 'this seems like it could confuse an LLM'. Each entry cites the actual incident it comes from.

A rule with a reliable mechanical trigger is packaged as a language-rule. A trap that requires understanding author intent to detect is packaged as an article instead of forced into the rule schema with a weak or false-positive-prone trigger.
